mappings.note: Acts of Union 1707 table: which parliaments, which new kingdom. Britain being made is LO-3; filling a table from memory is C-1.1
William I proclaimed at Versailles, the closing act of German unification, so LO-3 and not LO-2; a single name is C-1.1
asks what liberalism meant as a doctrine, an ism as an idea, which is LO-2; it does not ask how any state was built, which is what would send it to LO-3

serfdom abolished after 1848 because monarchs conceded to the liberal-nationalist revolts: the movements of the time and their effect, LO-2. The item weighs cause against effect, so no recall competency is added
names the French Revolution as nationalism's first expression, the opening claim of LO-1; LO-3 would be the right code only if a resulting European state were the subject

four claims about the 'Club of Thinkers' caricature, one of them (that it shows a liberal meeting) only refutable by looking at what the cartoon actually mocks; content is post-Vienna censorship (LO-2), source-reading takes C-1.2
Metternich's line about France sneezing is attributed, not explained; it is placed with the conservative order of LO-2 rather than LO-1, because the revolution it refers to is July 1830, not 1789
which nation Ireland was not part of in 1707: the composition of the British state, LO-3, recalled
the outcome of the Act of Union, again the making of the British state; distractors are all about who seized power from whom, so the demand is still retrieval
same German Emperor fact as item 27 in a different stem; identical mapping is correct here because the two items genuinely test the same thing
four unifiers matched to four roles in making Italy, so LO-3; Mazzini appears as a unifier rather than as founder of a society, which is what keeps it off LO-2

the woman question inside the liberal movement, and the reason offered is false, so the student must weigh it against what the movement actually did. That is LO-2's 'nature of the diverse social movements', argued not recalled
why Bismarck is called the architect: all four options are rival explanations of the process, so this is the analysis LO-3 names, unlike the William I items which only ask for a name
distinguishes Huebner's fallen Germania from Clasen's Germania guarding the Rhine, which can only be done by reading the supplied picture; allegory content sits on LO-3 and the image work on C-1.2
Young Italy is a secret society of the 1830s, the same LO-2 family as Young Europe, and deliberately not LO-3, where Mazzini sits when the question is about Italy being unified
1688, 1707, 1798 and 1801 all belong to the building of the British state, so the whole sequence is LO-3 with no second content family to split it
Renan's argument is about what a nation is, which is the idea-of-nationalism half of LO-3; the item only asks for his name, so C-1.1 and not the analysis reading
the detail that the statue in Sorrieu's print is Liberty, not unity; no picture is put before the student here, so unlike item 5 this is recall of the print's content and takes C-1.1 not C-1.2
the stem already names Marianne, so the stamp is decoration and the only demand is knowing she personifies France; allegory content is LO-3 but the image contributes nothing, hence C-1.1
defines what a nation state is, the concept LO-3 is built around; the distractors turn on absolute rule and on language alone, so it is a definition retrieved rather than a case analysed
links Sardinia-Piedmont's wars to the economic motive of its ruling elites, a cause-and-effect judgement about Italy being made; LO-3 carries it without a recall competency

matches Germania's broken chains, eagle breastplate, sword and rising sun to their meanings; this is the memorised symbol key of the textbook table, so C-1.1, not the C-1.2 reserved for items where a picture must be read

defines plebiscite, the instrument by which Nice and Savoy joined Italy, so its content home is nation-state formation; a term definition is C-1.1. Weak content anchor: the frame has no outcome for historical vocabulary

identifies the landed aristocracy by its estates, French speech and marriage ties. Nearest legal home is LO-2, the social composition behind the movements; the frame has no outcome for the social structure of pre-1848 Europe, so this fit is thin
word-for-word repeat of item 28 on what liberal nationalism signified; same ism-as-idea reading, so the same LO-2 plus recall
